technical-summary: Eliminated the cross-component consolidated tool catalog from the system prompt: removed derive_harness_instructions and check_harness_instruction_drift from runtime/harness/system_prompt.py, stopped the loader from deriving harness-instructions (now empty unless a component supplies an explicit section), and removed the empty '## MCP tools' section from the pi SYSTEM.md template. Deduplicated component MCP configs so per-tool definitions are owned solely by each component's tool-descriptions (MCP-advertised): dropped the dead 'What you can do' harness-instructions catalogs in planning/agents/memory and the 'Official MCP servers'/'operating rules' blocks in source-control/coding-lsp (these matched no live template header and duplicated tool-descriptions), and trimmed server 'instructions' to cross-tool doctrine only. Updated loader-id tests to assert no derived catalog and that explicit harness-instructions survive; updated dynamic-agent-config test to assert 'MCP tools' is no longer injected. Preserved test-pinned text (list_components in project instructions, CLI visibility in session instructions).
user-summary-candidate: Slimmed MCP tooling config so each component owns its own tool definitions and the agent system prompt no longer carries a duplicated, cross-component tool catalog — reducing context with no loss of tool discoverability (tools are advertised directly over MCP).

technical-summary: Slimmed the hindsight recipes monolith (1247→1042 lines, -205) by extracting shared scaffolding. Added ProviderRecipeResult.with_metadata() to the providers layer — a dataclasses.replace-based helper that overlays source_url/source_date/action_needed onto any result (None preserves existing). Added a local _RowRecipe mixin holding the per-provider metadata constructor (provider_id, capability_id='hindsight', backend_id, recipe_kind, display_name, source_url, source_date, _row) plus _stamp(result) = with_metadata(action_needed=result.action_needed or row.audia_action). All six recipe classes now inherit the mixin, collapsing six identical ~8-line constructors. _McpConfigAdapter dropped from ~115 lines of hand-rebuilt results to one-line _stamp delegations; PluginConfigRecipe delegations and dry_run likewise. Added _run_command() to dedupe the parameterize→split→subprocess→returncode block previously copied four times across HooksInstaller/PluginConfig install/uninstall. Behavior preserved: HindsightMcpRecipe never sets action_needed so adapter results still resolve to audia_action; _stamp now also carries through error/details (previously dropped in some branches — strictly more complete). Public API exercised by tests unchanged.
user-summary-candidate: Refactored the Hindsight provider-integration recipes to reuse shared provider-recipe code, cutting ~200 lines of duplicated boilerplate with no behavior change.

technical-summary: Migrated agent-jobs and planning state handling to config-driven definitions backed by shared foundation logic. Added foundation/workflow/transitions.py: a slim host-agnostic module with load_workflow(path,kind,name) plus is_known_state/transition_allowed/states_in_set/in_state_set predicates; refactored StateMachine.state to reuse the predicates (deduping its inline check). agent-jobs: new component-local workflows.yaml defines the job lifecycle (states+transitions+terminal set); state_machine.py now derives LEGAL_TRANSITIONS/TERMINAL_STATES from it and validates via the shared predicates, preserving the public API (transition_job/transition_and_persist) and agent-jobs error kind/codes. planning: new component-local workflows.yaml defines item (pending<->completed) and review (created/considered/closed) workflows; planning_api set_state/set_review_state validate transitions via a thin _check_transition helper using the shared predicates, while the component keeps folder placement and input-alias handling. Added the two workflow YAMLs to setuptools package-data. Components stay segregated (own storage + error contracts); only transition-table semantics are shared.
user-summary-candidate: Job and planning state transitions are now defined in per-component workflow config files and validated through shared workflow logic, replacing hardcoded transition tables.

technical-summary: Wired automatic Hindsight provisioning across providers when the memory backend is configured, and fixed two latent recipe bugs surfaced by an end-to-end proof. Bug fixes: (1) _stamp assumed inner results were ProviderRecipeResult, but HindsightMcpRecipe returns the foundation RecipeResult — _stamp now builds a ProviderRecipeResult from duck-typed fields (removed the unused with_metadata helper that was the footgun); (2) _resolve_harness_config_path ignored project_root and wrote MCP config relative to CWD — now anchored via _absolute_project_path. Added a regression test exercising the MCP-adapter path + project_root anchoring (the previously-uncovered gap). Auto-wiring (encapsulated): new hindsight/provision.reconcile_hindsight(project_root, provider_ids) (implementation owns the matrix; applies when backend configured, tears down with a placeholder backend otherwise); new runtime/lifecycle/provider_recipes.refresh_provider_recipes() composition bridge — the only code knowing both providers (generic enabled-provider query) and the memory implementation; memory_mcp set_config/select_implementation now consume the needs_provider_recipe_refresh hint via the bridge (best-effort). providers component is untouched and never imports memory/Hindsight; memory_api stays provider-agnostic. Tests: unit provisioner/bridge tests + a parametrized per-provider integration test validating config/rule files are written and reverted (round-trip), runnable in the standard Docker suite.
user-summary-candidate: Configuring a memory backend now automatically installs Hindsight into all enabled providers (and removes it when unconfigured), with per-provider tests validating each provider's files are written and reverted correctly. Also fixed two provisioning bugs that wrote to the wrong location and broke MCP-config providers.

technical-summary: Reverted an over-engineered allow_install/MCP-downgrade detour and aligned Hindsight provisioning with the intended model: when the memory backend is configured, each provider runs its native installer if it has one, else gets MCP/rules config pointing at the external server. Replaced the bespoke _run_command (which rejected '&&'/'|' shell-compound syntax) with one that splits the matrix install command on '&&' into a SequenceStep of ShellSteps from the existing foundation toolchain (foundation.workflow.invocation.steps), with URL/TOKEN/KEY/ID substituted from the backend; genuine pipes/redirects are rejected with a clear message. Removed allow_install param from resolve_hindsight_strategy/register/apply/teardown/reconcile (kept the _external_fallback_row refactor for the platform gate). Installs now actually run on the live host via the shared step machinery (fail-fast across steps).
user-summary-candidate: Hindsight provider installs now run for real when the memory backend is configured — multi-step installer commands execute through the existing toolchain step machinery (pointed at your external server), and providers without a native installer get an MCP config instead.

technical-summary: Fixed the Hindsight MCP entry URL: build_hindsight_entry wrote the bare backend.base_url for http/sse transports, but that is the API root and does not speak MCP (returns 404); the MCP endpoint is base_url + /mcp. Switched the entry url to backend.mcp_url (idempotent property that appends /mcp). Installer recipes still use base_url for --api-url (the API root, per vendor docs), so only the MCP entry path changed. Updated four tests that had encoded the bare-URL bug. Verified end-to-end against a live Hindsight server: provisioning a provider writes url=<base>/mcp and an MCP initialize handshake to that exact URL succeeds (serverInfo hindsight-mcp-server 3.2.4).
user-summary-candidate: Fixed Hindsight MCP provider entries to point at the server's /mcp endpoint instead of the bare base URL, so providers actually connect (verified against a live server).

technical-summary: Added a per-provider Hindsight provisioning e2e test that runs in an isolated Docker harness (mutates_host, gated on AUDIAGENTIC_DOCKER_TESTS). It drives apply_hindsight per provider against a configured backend and validates the real artifacts, with an explicit spec per provider (no uniform behavior): mcp/hybrid providers (gemini, copilot, openhands, roo) assert a config entry referencing <server>/mcp; cline asserts its real published installer (pip install hindsight-cline && hindsight-cline install --api-url ... --api-token ...) wrote ~/.hindsight/cline.json referencing the server (cline is platform-gated: MCP on Windows, real hooks installer on Linux); qwen asserts a managed rule block; and codex/claude/opencode/aider/continue/goose/local-openai/plandex/pi are skipped with concrete reasons (shell-pipe installer, needs claude CLI, manual instruction, package unpublished on PyPI, adapter-service architecture, no integration). New Dockerfile.hindsight-provider-e2e (from audia-test-base) sets PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES=1 and installs tomli-w (OpenHands TOML writer dep). Registered in run_all.py RECIPE_IMAGES. Result in Docker: 6 passed, 9 skipped; 15 skipped locally (gated).
user-summary-candidate: Added a Docker test that provisions Hindsight for each provider and validates the files written — including running cline's real installer in isolation — with explicit, reasoned skips for providers that can't be tested yet.

Updated the Hindsight matrix so Continue stays config-managed and Roo carries concrete API installer args.

technical-summary: Added a generic configuration-completeness derivation to foundation/features. OptionSchema now carries required + description (previously parsed from YAML then discarded). New config_status.py provides evaluate_config (pure, schema+options -> configured/missing_required/effective_options) and implementation_config_status (state-backed, generic across any implementation-backed component). memory_status adopts the helper, replacing the ad-hoc bool(enabled or options) heuristic with schema-driven completeness and surfacing missing_required with descriptions. memory.yaml declares a status-hook; the component status CLI now invokes the generic get_component_status and includes a detail block for any component with a status hook. No component-specific logic added to foundation. First adopter (memory) as proof; planning/coding-lsp/providers rollout pending review.
user-summary-candidate: Memory (and any configurable component) now reports what configuration it still needs. Running component status on memory shows configured=false with the specific missing option (base-url) and its description, instead of a silent unconfigured state.

technical-summary: Adopted the shared config-completeness helper in planning. Extracted active_implementation_id + planning_status into planning_api.py (thin-MCP pattern); planning_manage_mcp's status tool and _active_implementation now delegate. planning_status returns standardized enabled/configured/missing_required fields via implementation_config_status alongside item counts. planning.yaml declares a status-hook so the component status CLI surfaces the same detail block. coding-lsp and providers intentionally NOT migrated: their readiness (running language servers / CLI+auth health) is a different axis than options-schema completeness and keeps its own logic.
user-summary-candidate: Planning now reports the same standardized configuration status as memory (active implementation, enabled, configured) through component status, using one shared derivation rather than a bespoke per-component rule.

technical-summary: Removed the memory-specific coupling from the runtime layer: runtime/lifecycle/provider_recipes.py is now a generic capability reconciler registry (register_provider_recipe_reconciler / refresh_provider_recipes) that imports no component; memory self-registers its Hindsight reconciler via a new lifecycle-observer module (memory_observer.py) wired through memory.yaml. Also: fixed a Windows subprocess decode crash by forcing utf-8/errors=replace in foundation ShellStep and the recipe shell path; guidance-only providers (e.g. pi) now report a clean skip instead of an error via a GuidanceOnlyRecipe.provision no-op; reconcile now prunes stale Hindsight config from disabled providers (config-only prune, never destructive uninstall commands); memory_set_config surfaces a provider_integration_summary; Hindsight options schema switched to host (required) + port (default 8888) + scheme (default http), with base_url composed in build_hindsight_backend and a read-time fallback for legacy base-url configs.
user-summary-candidate: Configuring memory now only needs a host (port defaults to 8888), reports a clear per-provider integration summary, cleanly skips providers with no Hindsight integration, removes stale integration from disabled providers, and no longer crashes on Windows installer output. Reversal (teardown/prune) is available for every provider.

technical-summary: Fixed wheel-only path resolution regressions in launcher install dispatch, provider action config loading, and schema lookup; packaged required managed skill/workflow assets so component install and release bootstrap validate from built wheels; aligned packaging image pytest config/plugins and kept low-value MCP subprocess suites opt-in.
user-summary-candidate: Stabilized install and packaging regressions so wheel-based component, MCP, and provider validation now exercise real behavior instead of failing on source-tree assumptions.

technical-summary: Made memory 'enabled' the real on/off switch for provider integration, orthogonal to 'configured'. reconcile_hindsight gained an `active` flag: when active+configured it installs to enabled providers and prunes stale from the rest; when disabled (active=False) or unconfigured it uninstalls (teardown) from ALL providers via all_provider_ids, while leaving the Hindsight config/options untouched so a later enable reinstalls. memory_observer._reconcile computes active from is_enabled(memory) and no longer skips when disabled (it tears down instead); it also subscribes to lifecycle.component.* events so enabling/disabling the memory component triggers reconciliation (install on enable, uninstall-all on disable). build_hindsight_backend stays a pure config resolver so config persists across disable.
user-summary-candidate: Memory's enabled state now genuinely controls provider integration: disabling uninstalls Hindsight from every provider while keeping your configuration, and re-enabling reinstalls it across providers. Configured and enabled are independent — a configured backend can be switched off and back on without reconfiguring.

technical-summary: Fixed two Windows-only execution bugs in the shared command runner and a Hindsight teardown gap. (1) ShellStep now resolves command[0] via shutil.which before Popen so Windows executes npm/.cmd/.bat shims (bare Popen(['claude',...]) failed with WinError 2 because it does not apply PATHEXT); no-op on POSIX. (2) ShellStep and the recipe shell path force encoding=utf-8/errors=replace so installer output containing non-cp1252 glyphs (checkmark, ellipsis) no longer crashes the reader thread. (3) claude's Hindsight matrix row had an empty uninstall_command, so teardown ran config-prune, found nothing, and falsely reported 'absent' while the plugin stayed installed; added 'claude plugin uninstall hindsight-memory'. Verified live and non-persistently against real CLI state: apply installs the plugin, teardown removes it (claude plugin list confirms), env restored clean.
user-summary-candidate: Hindsight now installs and cleanly uninstalls for Claude (and other CLI-driven providers) on Windows. Fixed a crash on installer output with special characters, a Windows path-resolution failure that prevented installers from running at all, and a gap where disabling did not actually remove the Claude plugin.

technical-summary: Added an opt-in, host-runnable, non-persistent per-provider Hindsight validation that catches host-platform bugs the Docker-only e2e suite structurally cannot. Gated by AUDIAGENTIC_LIVE_PROVIDER_TESTS=1 (marked opt_in + slow, skipped by default) and per-provider CLI presence. Redirects HOME/USERPROFILE to a tmp dir so real installers write there and the developer's real home is never touched; every case tears down in finally and asserts the integration is actually gone. Assertions observe real state (claude plugin list, provider MCP config file, provider-specific hooks artifact, managed rule block) rather than the recipe's self-report, so recipes that falsely report success or leave residue after teardown are caught. Verified it fails when the claude uninstall regression is reintroduced, and passes across the 11 installed providers on this host with the real home confirmed untouched.
user-summary-candidate: Added optional live per-provider tests that validate Hindsight install and teardown against the actual provider CLIs on the developer's machine, in an isolated home so they never modify the real environment. These catch platform-specific install failures and incomplete teardowns that the Docker-only tests miss.

technical-summary: Fix three related Windows/Claude Code MCP connectivity issues. (1) mcp_interpreter() now returns sys.executable unconditionally — pythonw.exe suppresses stdout which breaks all stdio MCP transports. (2) _resolve_mcp_path() and _absolute_project_path() now call .expanduser() so '~'-prefixed paths resolve correctly. (3) claude.yaml mcp_config.config_path changed from '.mcp.json' (project-local) to '~/.claude/mcp.json' (global Claude Code config) so AUDiaGentic MCP servers are available in all Claude Code sessions. (4) Added plugin_url_config_path field to HindsightRecipeRow and hindsight_matrix.yaml; claude's hindsight recipe now builds _ClaudePluginUrlRecipe which writes {"hindsightApiUrl": backend.base_url} to ~/.hindsight/claude-code.json (URL from config, never hardcoded) instead of attempting an MCP JSON write. (5) _repair_windows_plugin_mcp() patches the Claude plugin's auto-generated .mcp.json from bash run_mcp.sh to python.exe mcp_server.py on Windows. Test suite updated with claude_home fixture to isolate HOME for all claude MCP path tests.
user-summary-candidate: Fix Claude Code MCP connectivity on Windows: servers were silently broken because pythonw.exe suppresses stdout (now uses python.exe), AUDiaGentic MCP servers now write to ~/.claude/mcp.json (globally available across all projects), and the Hindsight plugin now correctly writes its backend URL to ~/.hindsight/claude-code.json with a Windows repair for the bash→python.exe launcher issue.

technical-summary: Removed dead _run_command/_step_detail helpers and unused StepResult/ShellStep/SequenceStep imports from recipes.py. Updated 4 boundary tests to use install_steps/uninstall_steps instead of removed install_command/uninstall_command attributes on HindsightRecipeRow.
user-summary-candidate: Cleaned up dead code from Hindsight recipe migration: removed legacy _run_command helper, unused step model imports, and updated test assertions to match new ProvisionStep contract.

technical-summary: Added provision_steps() to all Hindsight recipe classes: HooksInstallerRecipe, PluginConfigRecipe, _ClaudePluginUrlRecipe, RulesOnlyRecipe, _McpConfigAdapter, _CompositeRecipe. Each returns a list of ProvisionStep instances for CompensatingSequence execution. Added _hindsight_params_for_rules helper. Imported ManagedBlockStep from provision_step module.
user-summary-candidate: Completed TO12 Phase E: All Hindsight recipes now expose provision_steps() for structured rollback-aware provisioning through CompensatingSequence.

technical-summary: HindsightMcpRecipe.prune() now also prunes the artifact registry when using a custom remover_fn. Previously, providers with provider-specific format callbacks (cline, gemini) removed the MCP entry from config but left artifacts.json with stale hindsight references, causing teardown to fail cleanup validation.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed Hindsight teardown for providers with custom MCP format handlers (Cline, Gemini) — artifact registry sidecar is now cleaned up on prune.

technical-summary: Cleaned repository root by removing test-related root files. Folded the root pytest path bootstrap into tests/conftest.py so pytest still adds the repository root and src/ to sys.path during test runs, then deleted the obsolete root conftest.py and stale run_tests.py wrapper now superseded by tests/run_all.py. Verified pytest collection and execution for tests/unit/contracts/test_validate_ids.py, and confirmed no root-level *test*.py files remain.
user-summary-candidate: Cleaned test-related files out of the repository root while preserving pytest imports; tests/run_all.py remains the supported test runner.

technical-summary: Implemented the Agent LLM Gateway (AG07-AG13): async/blocking/event-triggered submission of direct LLM completions, resolved through agent profiles to providers.services.execution.execute_provider. New gateway-owned request/result contract and persisted state store (agent-llm-record.schema.json, agents_gateway_store.py) deliberately not built on agent_jobs.JobRecord (see AG07 decision). Per-profile FIFO queue with strict concurrency (agents_gateway_queue.py), retry + cross-profile fallback classified by canonical error-code prefix (agents_gateway_dispatch.py), a public submit/status/wait/cancel/run API and dedicated audiagentic-scoped MCP server (agents_gateway_api.py/agents_gateway_mcp.py — not propagated to providers, avoiding a provider-surface re-entrancy risk), an agents.llm.requested event trigger (agents_gateway_events.py) publishing queued/started/completed/failed/cancelled/rejected lifecycle events for every request regardless of origin, and a ComponentStatusPayload status-hook (agents_api.agent_status) reporting profile count/default and gateway queue depths. Also fixed a real generator bug in planning_api._next_review_id (numbered per-plan while uniqueness is checked globally, causing review-ID collisions across plans) discovered while filing plan reviews for this work.
user-summary-candidate: Added an Agent LLM Gateway: submit direct LLM completion requests asynchronously, block for a result, or trigger them via events — with automatic retry and fallback across agent profiles.

technical-summary: Planning review state transitions and review deletion now invoke empty plan-directory cleanup. Cleanup prunes empty nested review folders before removing empty plan directories, preventing stale active/completed planning folders after all files move away. Existing empty active planning review directories were pruned.

Features now own language server dependencies, implementations own runtime dependencies, and bindings only say which implementation supports which feature and how to project it.

technical-summary: Rewrote Standard 1 (Layer Boundaries): foundation is now defined as the capability layer rather than a bottom primitives layer; a new runtime-environment namespace (runtime/system, read-only execution-context facts) is importable from any layer including foundation, generalizing the previous ad hoc runtime.system.platform exception; runtime orchestration (lifecycle/harness/config/state/rig/update) is defined as a quasi-composition root with soft guidance to prefer events/registries over direct capability calls after startup. Anti-pattern table updated: foundation-imports row now scopes to runtime orchestration (anything outside runtime/system) and a new row prohibits orchestration logic or upward imports inside runtime/system.
user-summary-candidate: Architecture doctrine updated: foundation is the capability layer and may read runtime-environment facts (runtime/system); runtime acts as a bootstrap/composition layer with import rules relaxed accordingly.

technical-summary: AR02: Generic capability registry eliminates 3 lazy imports of optional providers from foundation/runtime layers. Split loader validation into data-driven + contribution phases to honor bootstrap order. Seam A uses get_capability for surface validator; Seam B resolves MCP projector via registry; Seam C uses capability keys for provider config/descriptors.
user-summary-candidate: Foundation and runtime no longer import from the providers component — all cross-layer calls now go through a generic capability registry that gracefully degrades when providers is absent.
